content.title: Action movie star Chuck Norris dies at 86. His ties to Florida
content.text: March 20, 2026, 2:11 p.m. ETChuck Norris, the martial artist and action movie icon, died at age 86.Best known for his role in Bruce Lee's 1972 film "The Way of the Dragon" and the TV series "Walker, Texas Ranger," Norris in later years used his celebrity platform to champion conservative activism.His ties to Florida aren't deep, but he did star in the 1985 action movie "Invasion U.S.A.," in which a Soviet/Cuban-led terrorist force invades Florida. Parts of the movie included locales in Miami, Kendall and Fort Lauderdale although only a portion of that span was actually shot in Florida. Additional work on the movie happened around Fort Pierce.Norris reportedly showed up in Miami briefly for events and appearances.In the movie, Norris defended the United States as former CIA Agent Matt Hunter.Chuck Norris helped Floridians during Hurricane MiltonIn October 2024, Norris sent two dozen pallets of water from his Texas ranch to the Seminole County Office of Emergency Management after Hurricane Milton. County officials said the water was delivered to Harvest Time International in partnership with U.S. Rep. Cory Mills.There was a politician named Chuck Norris who died in West Palm BeachThere was an Oregon politician named Charles Reed “Chuck” Norris who retired to Royal Palm Beach in Palm Beach County in 2002 and died in West Palm Beach in 2009. He has not related to the martial-arts actor.Norris the politician served in the Oregon House of Representatives as a Republican from 1987 to 1997.Chuck Norris the actor promoted conservative politicsWhile never seeking elected office himself, the patriotic Norris used his celebrity platform to champion conservative activism, appearing in campaign ads, speaking at rallies and engaging with grassroots organizations. The actor drew controversy for a 2012 political ad with his wife, Gena, warning that President Barack Obama’s reelection could lead the country down a path they likened to “1,000 years of darkness.”Chuck Norris' film rolesNorris was cast by Bruce Lee as the villain Colt in Lee's 1972 film "The Way of the Dragon." Their fight scene, set in Rome's Colosseum, is one of the most famous martial arts screen fights and the rare screen battle that Norris lost (broken neck).The rising star appeared as tough Texas Ranger Jim "J.J." McQuade in 1983's “Lone Wolf McQuade," a character precursor to his famed "Walker, Texas Ranger" role.In the 1984 box office smash "Missing in Action," Norris portrayed one-man-army Colonel Braddock, who returns to Vietnam to free POWs. The next year, Norris starred in "Invasion U.S.A." The same mega-year, Norris starred as a Chicago police sergeant battling his way out of a gang war in "Code of Silence."Norris teamed with Lee Marvin in 1986's "The Delta Force," memorably wreaking solo havoc with a rocket-launching dirt bike in one of the action film's most over-the-top action sequences.Chuck Norris' TV rolesBy the 1990s, Norris transitioned from big-screen muscle to television icon, anchoring CBS' "Walker, Texas Ranger," where his blend of martial arts, moral clarity and frontier justice made him a household name across nine seasons (1993-2001) and introduced him to a new generation of fans.Later in life, Chuck Norris 'facts'As a senior citizen, Norris experienced an unlikely digital resurgence in the 2000s. A torrent of internet humor known as “Chuck Norris Facts” transformed the star into a mythical, near-invincible figure. The deadpan one-liners exaggerating his strength, speed and toughness to absurd levels, turned Norris into one of the internet’s first global memes. A typical example: "Chuck Norris doesn’t wear a watch. He decides what time it is."Chuck Norris teamed with Sylvester Stallone, Arnold SchwarzeneggerIn 2012, Norris played the mercenary Booker in "The Expendables 2," alongside fellow action screen legends Sylvester Stallone, Arnold Schwarzenegger and Jason Statham. Stallone wrote a scene which featured Booker dramatically saving the entire group of under-attack mercenaries on his own — the highest action star honor.As the smoke clears, Stallone's Barney Ross sets up a "Chuck Norris Fact" joke by asking Booker about a rumored cobra bite.“Yeah. After five days of agonizing pain…the cobra died," Booker responds.Family posts that Chuck Norris was 'a symbol of strength'Norris' family confirmed the death on Thursday, March 19, with a post to Instagram on Friday, March 20. No cause was cited."It is with heavy hearts that our family shares the sudden passing of our beloved Chuck Norris yesterday morning. While we would like to keep the circumstances private, please know that he was surrounded by his family and was at peace," the statement read. "To the world, he was a martial artist, actor, and a symbol of strength. To us, he was a devoted husband, a loving father and grandfather, an incredible brother, and the heart of our family.""He lived his life with faith, purpose, and an unwavering commitment to the people he loved," the statement continued. "Through his work, discipline, and kindness, he inspired millions around the world and left a lasting impact on so many lives."Norris is survived by his second wife, Gena O'Kelley, whom he married in 1998, and five children: sons Mike and Eric (with first wife Diane Holechek), twins Dakota and Danilee (with O'Kelley), and Dina (from a previous relationship).Chuck Norris was born in Oklahoma, moved to CaliforniaBorn Carlos Ray Norris on March 10, 1940, in Ryan, Oklahoma, Norris devoured the movies of John Wayne growing up. The actor told the New York Times in 1985 he regarded Wayne as his ''substitute father'' after his father, an alcoholic, left the family's home when he was 10. His mother later moved the family of three boys to Torrance, California.
